fullnameOverride.description: Override the fully qualified app name.

apiURL.description: GitHub API base URL; empty is api.github.com.

appID.description: Id of the read-only GitHub App `giantswarm-repo-manager-inventory`, the one identity of the unattended reads: the org sweep, the engine's checks in read mode and the name check of a dry run run as its installation, on its own rate budget. Its permissions, all read: Administration, Contents, Pull requests, Issues, Commit statuses (the `ci/circleci:` contexts on the default branch head), Checks (the check runs on the default branch head: the engine's protection step reads them to learn which conditional checks exist — without it every repository carries the finding `unchecked`, the checks on main not readable with this token), Metadata, Organization members. 0 leaves the unattended reads unconfigured — nothing stands in for the App; the tools that need it say so.

existingSecret.description: Existing Secret with the inventory App's PEM private key under `private-key`.

installationID.description: The inventory App's installation id on the org.

global.description: Platform-wide values an umbrella chart shares with every component and Helm forwards here; this chart reads none of them.

tag.description: Image tag. Defaults to the chart appVersion.

connectTimeout.description: How long the server waits for the store at start (a Go duration), retrying with backoff, before it gives up and exits; it serves meanwhile, liveness passing and readiness failing until the store answers, so a Valkey that starts after the manager — a volume binding late, a restart — costs no container restart within the window. `"0"` waits for ever.

org.description: The GitHub organization the inventory covers.

pollInterval.description: Read the reconciler workflow's completed runs from GitHub as the inventory App every interval (a Go duration) and store each run's `reconcile-<repository>` artifact as the repository's `setup.lastRun`; every 30 s while a Align now (`align_repository`) is pending. `"0"` turns the poller off. Nothing reaches the server from the workflow: the App needs Actions read on `teamFiles.repository`.

workflow.description: The reconciler's workflow file in `teamFiles.repository`: the one `align_repository` dispatches and the poller reads the runs of.

activeDays.description: Days within which a Renovate pull request or commit counts as Renovate activity — `list_repositories`' Renovate state `active`, else `inactive`. Passed as `RENOVATE_ACTIVE_DAYS`.

concurrency.description: Parallel engine reads during a sweep.

engineChecks.description: Run the engine's set-up checks in read mode for every accepted declaration during a sweep (REST as the App, about ten calls per repository). A `refresh_repository` always runs them.

graphqlBudgetFloor.description: Stop a sweep cleanly when the GraphQL budget's remaining points fall below this; 0 never stops.

interval.description: Full sweep over the org every interval (a Go duration); `"0"` turns the schedule off. The first sweep runs at start when the last one is older than the interval.

teams.description: GitHub team slugs whose members may start a sweep on demand with the tool `sweep_inventory` (membership checked on GitHub as the caller): the teams that own the manager and the reconciler. Passed as `SWEEP_TEAMS`.

valkeyAddress.description: Address (`host:port`) of the Valkey the inventory lives in, passed to the server as `VALKEY_ADDR`. Empty derives the subchart's Service, `<valkey.valkey.fullnameOverride>.<namespace>.svc:6379`; required when `valkey.enabled` is false.

auth.description: How muster authenticates to this server; rendered only with `oauth.enabled`: `auth.type: oauth` with the GitHub App `giantswarm-repo-manager` pinned as the authorization server — the pattern of the `github` and `pro` servers on the platform. GitHub publishes no discovery document, so the endpoints are named; the App's client credentials come from a Secret; no `scopes` for GitHub (the App's permissions are the App's), a `scopes` value for an authorization server that needs one. muster runs the consent once per person and puts their user token on every call.

name.description: Secret with the App's OAuth client under `client-id` and `client-secret`.

namespace.description: Namespace of that Secret; empty is the release namespace.

expectedIssuer.description: The issuer the authorization server puts in the RFC 9207 `iss` parameter of its authorization response — GitHub's is `https://github.com/login/oauth` for every App, while `issuer` stays the App's own identity the grant is filed under (muster#1277). Empty omits the field.

grantScope.description: `subject`: the grant belongs to the person, not to one login session — every session of theirs (the portal, an agent, a Slack click) carries the same token.

issuer.description: The issuer identity the person's grant is filed under: the App's own, so the login App's GitHub grant stays separate.

scopes.description: The OAuth `scope` parameter of the authorization request (space-separated), only for an authorization server that needs one — a Dex standing in for GitHub in a lab takes `openid profile email offline_access`. Leave empty for GitHub: a GitHub App's permissions are the App's, and the token endpoint takes no scope. Empty omits the field.

autoStart.description: Start the server connection when muster initializes.

enabled.description: Register this server with muster by rendering an `mcpservers.muster.giantswarm.io` CR in the release namespace. Tools then appear as `x_<name>_<tool>`.

labels.description: Extra labels on the MCPServer CR.

name.description: MCPServer CR name (drives the tool prefix).

timeout.description: Seconds muster waits for one call before it cancels it (the CR's `spec.timeout`; muster's own default is 30, the CRD allows 1–300). 180 because `create_repository` in `mode: commit` does its writes in one call — create the repository, fetch and render the template, push the scaffold, open the pull request — and `align_repository` and `set_lifecycle` with the ask come close to muster's default as well.

baseURL.description: URL muster reaches this server at, without the MCP path: the resource of its OAuth protected-resource metadata. Empty derives the in-cluster Service URL, `http://<fullname>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:<service.port>`.

enabled.description: Require a GitHub user token as the bearer of every MCP request, verified with `GET /user`; the server then acts as that person. Behind muster the token is the person's own: muster runs the consent for the GitHub App `giantswarm-repo-manager` once (the MCPServer's `authorizationServer` pin under `muster.mcpServer.auth`), stores and refreshes the user token and puts it on every call. Off: anonymous — no caller, nothing acts as a person, the tools say so; only for a server nothing but a trusted proxy can reach.

replicaCount.description: Number of replicas. The server holds its state in Valkey; more than one is fine.

audience.description: The audience of the projected token — the gateway's `reviews.audience`; this ServiceAccount must be in its `reviews.allowedCallers`.

channels.description: Slack channel IDs by the channel names a team's policy file carries: `slackChannel` (asks with an Approve button) and `standupChannel` (notices). The gateway takes IDs, so every channel a policy file names needs an entry (`team-x: C…`, `standup-x: C…`) unless the file carries the ID itself.

gatewayURL.description: klaus-gateway's base URL as reached from the pod (for example `http://klaus-gateway.agent-platform.svc:8080`): lifecycle and transfer asks go to `POST /reviews` into the team's `slackChannel`, notices (the giving team's transfer notice, what a reconciler run tells the team) to `POST /notices` into its `standupChannel`, authenticated with this pod's projected ServiceAccount token for `audience`. Empty leaves the asks undelivered; the tools say so and approving on GitHub stays equivalent.

ref.description: The branch the files are read from and pull requests target.

repository.description: The repository that holds the team files (`repositories/<team>.yaml`, the desired state) and the policy files (`repository-setup/<team>.yaml`); every write is a pull request against it, opened as the caller.

valkey.description: The inventory store: the Giant Swarm `valkey` app as a subchart (its values live under `valkey.valkey`, the upstream chart's). One replica on an RWO volume with `Recreate`, so a rollout does not deadlock on the volume; the store is a cache — every record is rebuilt from the team files and GitHub — so the restart gap costs nothing. Set `valkey.enabled: false` and `inventory.valkeyAddress` to use a Valkey outside the release.
